name: Cons Qty (per garment)
formula: Cons Qty = Total Cons Qty ÷ Cons per Item
explanation: Total Cons Qty is the material needed for a batch of "Cons per Item" garments. Dividing gives the consumption for one garment in Cons UOM.
example: 3 KG_Nis ÷ 2 garments = 1.5 KG_Nis per garment (WFX shows 1.5).

name: Loss factor
formula: Loss Factor = 1 ÷ (1 − Loss %)
explanation: The system first turns Loss % into a factor. Loss is taken out of the gross quantity, so the factor is a division, not a plain mark-up.

name: Cons incl Loss
formula: Cons incl Loss = Cons Qty × Loss Factor
explanation: Loss is the first step of the chain. With no loss the Loss Factor is 1 and Cons incl Loss = Cons Qty.

name: Cons incl Wastage
formula: Cons incl Wastage = Cons incl Loss + (Cons incl Loss × Wastage %)
explanation: Wastage is added as a mark-up on the quantity after loss. If only wastage is given, Cons incl Loss is just Cons Qty and the result is the total consumption.

name: Cons incl Shrinkage
formula: Cons incl Shrinkage = Cons incl Wastage ÷ (1 − Shrinkage %)
explanation: Shrinkage is the last step and, like loss, is a division. If only shrinkage is given it applies straight to Cons Qty and the result is the total consumption.

name: Final Consumption
formula: Final (Total) Consumption = result of the chain: Cons Qty × 1/(1 − Loss %) → + Wastage % → ÷ (1 − Shrinkage %)
explanation: The last figure of the chain is the total consumption MRP explodes and FPO uses. Each of loss, wastage and shrinkage is optional: when only one is filled the system applies just that step and its result becomes the total consumption.
example: Cons 2 with loss, wastage and shrinkage of 5 % each = 2.326870. Only wastage 5 % = 2.1. Only loss 5 % = 2.105263. Only shrinkage 5 % = 2.105263. Adi TShirt (NIS-59) N-8: 1.65 (WFX shows 1.65).

name: Cons UOM Price
formula: Cons UOM Price = Purchase Price × Conversion Factor (Purchase UOM → Cons UOM)
explanation: Fabric is bought per meter but consumed per KG_Nis. 1 KG_Nis = 1,000 meter, so one Cons UOM costs 1,000 purchase units.
example: 15 INR/meter × 1,000 = 15,000 INR per KG_Nis (WFX shows 15,000). Trims use the default factor 1 when no UOM conversion is maintained: T-1 (PCS → meter) 10 → 10, NS1-1 8 → 8, PP-1 4 → 4.

name: Line Value
formula: Value = Final Consumption × Cons UOM Price
explanation: Material cost of one garment for this BOM line in the line currency.

name: Value (CS Currency)
formula: Value (CS Curr) = Value × exchange rate (line currency → costing-sheet currency)
explanation: Converts the line value to the BOM costing currency. Flannel Shirt Adi (NIS-58) is INR on both sides, so the rate is 1.
open_question: Which exchange-rate table does WFX use (BOM date, company rate, or OC rate)?

name: Colour / Size Dependency "Used"
formula: Used = Yes when the style colour (size) is mapped to a material colour (size); otherwise [Not Used]
explanation: With dependency type "Table" each style colour is mapped individually. Unmapped colours generate no material demand in MRP.
example: Flannel Shirt Adi (NIS-58) has 7 style colours; only BALSAM TREE, Cosmic sky purple and Happy Pink are mapped → 3 colours used.

name: After Process Valid?
formula: Valid = "First process" when After Process is blank; else Yes if After Process exists earlier in the sequence
explanation: Guards the routing order so a process cannot depend on one that never runs.
example: Sewing after VCutting → Yes; VPacking after Sewing → Yes.

name: Process Rate
formula: Process Rate = Cost Of (Operations tab) × Production Time (Operations tab)
explanation: Each process is costed from its operation: the cost per unit of time multiplied by the production time.
example: Adi TShirt (NIS-59): VCutting 3 × 100 = 300 · Sewing 2 × 5 = 10 · VPacking 3 × 5 = 15 (all match the Processes tab).
open_question: Described as "Cost Of + Production Time", but the screen only matches multiplication (3 + 100 = 103 ≠ 300). Confirm it is ×. (Cost Of is the default rate per unit of time; Efficiency % at default does not change the rate.)

name: Material Linkage
formula: Each BOM material line is linked to the routing process that consumes it
explanation: Tells WFX which process the material is issued to; production indents show it as "Required For".
example: Adi TShirt (NIS-59): N-8 → VCutting · T-1 and NS1-1 → Sewing · PP-1 → VPacking.

name: Section Total Cost
formula: Section Total Cost = Σ Value (CS Curr) of the lines in the section
explanation: Shown on each section header of the Cost tab, next to Budget and Additional Cost.
example: Adi TShirt (NIS-59) Fabric: 24,750 · Trim: 20.40 + 16.32 + 4.00 = 40.72 (WFX shows 24,750 Rs and 40.72 Rs).

name: Material Cost
formula: Material Cost = Σ section Total Cost (Fabric, Service, Yarn, Misc, Trim)
explanation: Each section total is the sum of BOM line Value (CS Curr) in that section.

name: Production Cost
formula: Production Cost = Σ routing Process Rate
explanation: Sum of the process rates on the routing (basis Amount).
example: VCutting 300 + Sewing 10 + VPacking 15 = 325 (same routing on Flannel Shirt Adi (NIS-58) and Adi TShirt (NIS-59)).

name: Total Cost
formula: Total Cost = Material + Production + Recipe + Indirect + CM
explanation: Full cost per piece used for profit and markup.

name: Net Selling Price
formula: Net Selling Price = Selling Price × (1 − Discount % ÷ 100)
explanation: Discount is a percentage of the selling price; WFX shows the amount under the %.

name: Profit
formula: Profit = Net Selling Price − Total Cost
explanation: Negative profit means the style is costed above its selling price.

name: Profit %
formula: Profit % = Profit ÷ Net Selling Price × 100
explanation: Margin on the selling price after discount. The small figure next to it (21 %) is the Target Profit %.
example: Adi TShirt (NIS-59): −21,515.72 ÷ 3,600 = −597.66 % (WFX shows −597.66 %). Flannel Shirt Adi (NIS-58) Excel recorded the ratio −6.6083.

name: Markup %
formula: Markup = Selling Price − Total Cost;  Markup % = Markup ÷ Total Cost × 100
explanation: Mark-up over cost uses the selling price BEFORE discount, unlike Profit which uses the price after discount.
example: Adi TShirt (NIS-59): 4,000 − 25,115.72 = −21,115.72; ÷ 25,115.72 = −84.07 % (WFX shows both). Flannel Shirt Adi (NIS-58) (no discount): −0.8686.
open_question: Markup ignores the discount while Profit applies it – is that intended?

name: Material Line Value
formula: Value = Units × Rate
explanation: Booked material value per colour/size line.

name: Balance to Indent
formula: Balance to Indent = Units − Indented Qty
explanation: How much of the booking is still to be indented. 0 means the booking is fully indented.

name: Balance Units
formula: Balance Units = Booked Units − Previous Indent Qty
explanation: Caps how much can still be indented against the booking line.

name: Open Qty & Status
formula: Open Qty = Indent Qty − Ordered Qty − In-house Adj. − On Order Adj.; Status = Completed when Open Qty = 0
explanation: Open qty is the part of the indent not yet covered by a PO or by stock.

name: PO Line Value
formula: Total Value = Ordered Qty × Price per Unit; Total Net Value = Total Value + Surcharge Value
explanation: Value is computed on the PO price, not the indent rate.

name: Open Qty
formula: Open Qty = Ordered Qty + Additional Qty − Shipped (GRN accepted) Qty
explanation: Shipped Qty is updated back from GRN.

name: Qty in Storing UOM
formula: Qty (Storing UOM) = Ordered Qty × PO-to-Storing UOM Conversion
explanation: Converts PO qty to the UOM stock is kept in.

name: Balance Qty
formula: Balance Qty = Ordered Qty − Previously Received Qty + Returned Qty
explanation: What can still be received against the PO line.

name: Accepted Qty & Value
formula: Accepted Qty = Received Qty − Rejected Qty; Value = Accepted Qty × Rate
explanation: Only accepted qty enters stock and updates RMPO Shipped Qty.

name: Excess / Short
formula: Excess/Short = Received Qty − Balance Qty
explanation: Positive = over-receipt (checked against shipment tolerance %), negative = short receipt.

name: Breakup Value
formula: Total Value = Qty × (Selling Price + CM Price)
explanation: Colour × size value of the delivery OC.
example: 300 × 33.3333 = 9,999.99 for Cosmic sky purple / Small; OC total 33,333.30 USD.

name: Level 1 Req Qty (garment)
formula: Req Qty = Actual Requirement × MRP % × (1 + Loss % ÷ 100)
explanation: Actual Requirement is the OC colour/size qty. MRP % = 1 means 100 %.
open_question: Confirm MRP % is a multiplier (1 = 100 %) and that Loss % at Level 1 is additive on top of it.

name: Level 2 Actual Requirement (fabric)
formula: Actual Requirement = Garment Req Qty × BOM Final Consumption (for the mapped material colour/size)
explanation: BOM explosion: each garment colour/size line is multiplied by the final consumption of every BOM material that is "Used" for that colour and size.
example: 200 × 1.5 = 300 KG_Nis for BALSAM TREE / Medium; total 1,500.

name: Demand Type split
formula: Production Qty when the item is manufactured (has a lower BOM level); Purchase Qty when it is bought. Net = Req Qty − Available Stock − Open Purchase
explanation: Level 1 garment → Production demand → Production Order. Level 2 fabric → Purchase demand → RMPO.

name: MRP adjustment (negative quantity)
formula: Entered at the parent: Net Parent Qty = Parent Qty + Adjustment; Child Indent Qty = Net Parent Qty × BOM Final Consumption. Entered at a child level: only that level changes (Child Qty + Adjustment).
explanation: Every MRP level can take a negative quantity. A child indent is reduced or cancelled only by a negative at its parent level, and it takes effect when MRP is re-run: any change in the parent followed by a re-run of MRP impacts the child indent. Taking off the whole parent quantity (-500 of 500) cancels it.
example: Level 1 = 500, Final Consumption 1.5: no adjustment → 750; -200 at Level 1, re-run MRP → 300 × 1.5 = 450; -500 at Level 1, re-run MRP → 0 (cancelled); -200 at Level 2 → fabric 550, Level 1 stays 500.

name: Split by percentage
formula: Split Quantity = Existing Quantity × Split Percentage ÷ 100 (per article colour/size line, rounded to the UOM precision); Remaining = Existing − Split
explanation: Per the Sales Order specification. The percentage must be above 0 and not above 100; the remaining quantity stays in the source delivery.
example: 20 % of Red/S 100, Red/M 200, Red/L 200 moves 20, 40 and 40.

name: Split by quantity
formula: Line Split Qty = Entered Quantity × Line Qty ÷ Total of the selected lines
explanation: The entered quantity is spread proportionately over the selected colour/size lines (specification wording: "distributed proportionately"). Quantity must be above zero and not above the delivery quantity.

name: Final Selling Price (upcharge / discount)
formula: Final Selling Price = Base Selling Price ± Upcharge/Discount (positive = upcharge, negative = discount)
explanation: Base price comes from the Tech Pack; the final price is read-only and recalculated whenever the upcharge or discount changes. Only when "Enable Base Price and Upcharge in Summary OC" is ON.

name: Sub Total (sales order currency)
formula: Sub Total = Delivery Value × Exchange Rate to the Sales Order Currency
explanation: Print and Proforma Invoice show a Sub Total column in the sales order currency, grouped at delivery / OC level.
example: 800 USD at 1 USD = 84 INR = 67,200 INR. 600 VDN at 1 INR = 300 VDN is about 2 INR (the specification shows 1.98).

name: OC Delivery Date from ex-factory days
formula: OC Delivery Date = Buyer Delivery Date − Ex-factory days (master by shipment mode, order company, buyer and buyer department)
explanation: Fills as soon as the Buyer Delivery Date is entered. Without a master entry the OC Delivery Date equals the Buyer Delivery Date.

name: Approval value rule
formula: Limit 0 → never approval; Limit -1 → always approval; Limit > 0 → approval only if Order Value > Limit
explanation: A value equal to the limit does not go for approval.
example: Limit 1,000: order 1,000 → no approval; order 1,500 → approval.

name: Material indents after Purchase Demand
formula: Material Indent Qty = (Level 1 Style Qty − Purchase Demand) × BOM Final Consumption
explanation: Purchase Demand at Level 1 is style quantity bought finished. On the next MRP run the material indents shrink by it; with the whole quantity there are none. The style indent with purchase demand goes to an RMPO.

name: Pieces from prepack ratio
formula: Solid Color / Assorted Size: PCS = PP × Size + PP × Size … ; Multiple Prepack: PCS = PP × TBA
explanation: Wording of the specification. Worked here as pack ratio per size × number of packs.
example: Ratio 1:2:1 over S/M/L with 10 packs = 10 + 20 + 10 = 40 pcs.
open_question: Confirm what "Size" and "TBA" stand for in PCS = PP × Size and PCS = PP × TBA (ratio × packs?).

name: Desync price check
formula: Desynced when OC Selling Price ≠ Cost Sheet / BOM Selling Price for the style and destination; Sync sets OC Selling Price = Cost Sheet / BOM Selling Price
explanation: The cost sheet or BOM is the source of truth. Update OC with latest cost sheet price re-reads a revised confirmed price.
example: Cost sheet 10, OC 20 → desynced → sync gives OC 10; cost sheet revised to 15 → update gives OC 15.

name: Purchase UOM Indent Qty
formula: Purchase UOM Indent Qty = Indent Qty × Conversion Factor
explanation: Indent qty is in Cons UOM (KG_Nis); the supplier is paid per meter.

name: In-house Adj. (from BBB stock)
formula: In-house Adj. = MIN(Indent Qty, BBB stock available for the same Stock Key)
explanation: Stock received earlier against block booking PPJ179 for the same article|colour|size is reserved automatically.

name: Ordered Qty (to RMPO)
formula: Ordered Qty = Indent Qty − In-house Adj. − On Order Adj.
explanation: Only the uncovered part goes to a new purchase order (RMPO 1230).

name: Indent Price
formula: Price = BOM Cons UOM Price
explanation: Production indents carry the BOM price per Cons UOM.

name: Allocated to FPO
formula: Allocated = Colour Qty × Qty % ÷ 100
explanation: Qty % lets planning push less than the OC qty into the factory order.

name: FPO Qty
formula: FPO Qty = Allocated Qty − Reduced at FPO
explanation: Quantity released to the factory per colour/size.

name: Fabric Qty Reqd
formula: Fabric Qty Reqd = FPO Qty × BOM Final Consumption
explanation: Same explosion as MRP Level 2 but on FPO qty.

name: Material Allocation Open Qty
formula: Open Qty = Qty Reqd − Net Qty Instructed (Qty Instructed − Qty Unreserved)
explanation: Qty Instructed is stock already reserved (the BBB in-house adjustment).

name: FPPO Open Qty
formula: Open Qty = Required Qty − Received Qty − Reallocation Qty
explanation: Every routing process gets the full FPO qty per colour/size as required qty.
open_question: Does Ordered Qty (issued to a contractor) reduce FPPO Open Qty, or only Received Qty?
